# Research

## Job Market Paper

[Late Medieval Unrest in the Holy Roman Empire: Climate, Institutions, and Documented Unrest](https://patrickjcrawford.github.io/files/Crawford_HRE-Unrest_Draft.pdf)

```{=latex}
\vspace{-0.4em}
\begin{small}
```
*Abstract:* I construct two linked datasets for the Holy Roman Empire, 1300--1520: a geolocated catalog of popular unrest and an annual panel of city-council representation across 306 cities. Contrary to prior work's positive drought association, documented unrest tends to be more frequent in wetter years. Guild representation's apparent associations with unrest come from the years in which representation changed, often as unrest's outcome; where guilds already held seats, severe drought went with less unrest.
```{=latex}
\end{small}
```
